canonical_statement: If probability measures mu_n converge weakly to mu and f is continuous, then the pushforward measures map f mu_n converge weakly to map f mu.

canonical_formal_target.declaration_or_expression: TBD: weak convergence of probability measures preserved by Measure.map along a continuous map

domain_and_universes: Provisional: topological measurable spaces alpha and beta; probability measures mu_n, mu on alpha; f : alpha -> beta
quantifiers: alpha beta : Type (universes to be frozen during statement phase)
mu : Measure alpha and mu_n : Nat -> Measure alpha
hypotheses: mu and every mu_n are probability measures
measurability/Borel compatibility required for Measure.map, to be minimized during statement elaboration
conclusion: Measure.map f (mu_n n) converges weakly to Measure.map f mu

alternate_encodings.target: random variables X_n, X with convergence in distribution; continuous f; f(X_n) converges in distribution to f(X)
alternate_encodings.checked_witness: none; transport is deferred to statement phase

alternate_encodings.relationship: strict generalization, intentionally excluded from the frozen root

excluded_degenerate_cases: The root does not claim the stronger almost-everywhere continuity theorem, varying maps, or convergence modes stronger than weak convergence. Constant maps and Dirac measures remain included boundary cases.
